findings.issue_text: `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:3` — `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. `force: true` issues a `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS` before creating. In a migration this is never right; on any re-run or partially-migrated DB it destroys data silently. Remove `force: true`.

`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:8-10` — `execute(...)[0]['id']` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method [] for nil` when the `embed_category` setting row doesn't exist or doesn't match a category name (the overwhelmingly common case — most sites never set `embed_category`). The migration will crash on upgrade for nearly every install. Guard the result the same way `embeddable_hosts` is guarded below (`res = execute(...); category_id = res.ntuples > 0 ? ... : 0`). Same problem on line 14 for `uncategorized_category_id` (that row usually exists, but it's the same unchecked pattern).

`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` — `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` interpolates a user-controlled site setting value directly into SQL. A host containing `'` breaks the migration; worse, it's SQL injection from stored settings. Use a bind/`quote`: `execute "INSERT ... VALUES (#{ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)}, ...)"`.

`db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb:25` vs `app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8` — migrated rows are inserted raw, so legacy values like `http://discourse.org` or `example.com/1234` keep their scheme/path, while `record_for_host` matches against `URI(url).host` (bare hostname). Every migrated host with a scheme prefix will silently stop allowing embeds after upgrade — a functional regression for existing customers. Normalize (`sub(%r{^https?://}, '').sub(%r{/.*$}, '')`) in the migration before inserting.

`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:16` — `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` never downcases the right-hand side. A referer of `http://EvilTrout.com/x` yields `host = "EvilTrout.com"`, which never matches `lower(host)`. Use `host.downcase`.

`app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:9-18` — `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can be `nil`; `update` then calls `host.host =` and `destroy` calls `host.destroy`, producing a 500 `NoMethodError` on any stale/bogus id (trivially reachable by two admins editing concurrently). Use `find` (404) or return `render_json_error` on nil.

`app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-7` — `before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` unconditionally; a record created without a host (`EmbeddableHost.new.save`, which the create endpoint permits if `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` is missing) raises `NoMethodError` on nil instead of failing validation. Guard with `return if host.blank?`, and note `sub!` mutates the string in place — safer to use `self.host = host.sub(...)`.

`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb:9-11` — `update` does nothing at all; it just re-renders. The controller's `saveChanges` action (`admin-embedding.js.es6:6`) therefore posts a no-op, and `embedding.hbs` never renders a save button anyway. Either implement or delete both the route/action and the client action; shipping a dead `PUT` endpoint is a maintenance trap.

`app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:22-24` — parameters are read directly off `params` with no strong-params permit and, more importantly, `category_id` is accepted unvalidated: there's no check the category exists, so a bad id yields either a FK-less orphan row (the migration adds no foreign key or index on `category_id`) or a confusing failure. Add `validates_presence_of :category_id` / `belongs_to` existence validation, and an index on `host`.

`app/models/topic_embed.rb:36,43` — `category: eh.try(:category_id)` passes an integer where the previous value was `SiteSetting.embed_category`, a category *name*. Discourse's `PostCreator`/`TopicCreator` `:category` option historically resolves by name (`Category.query_category`), so an integer may silently fall through to uncategorized. Verify against `PostCreator` (not present in this checkout) and switch to the option that takes an id (`category_id`) if so. Also, when `eh` is nil (import for a non-registered host) the topic now lands in uncategorized with no warning.

`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` / `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` — the two files' contents are swapped: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines all the category fabricators. This almost certainly happened by accident. Fabrication resolves by scanning the path so tests may still pass, but any lazy/by-name lookup breaks and it is deeply confusing. Swap them back.

`spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`, `spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` — the only tests assert class ancestry (`< Admin::AdminController`). There is no coverage of create/update/destroy, host normalization, `record_for_host` matching (case, scheme, port, path), or the migration. Given issues 4/5 above are exactly the untested paths, add model specs for `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` at minimum.

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22` — `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first underscore; a future multi-word admin model (`foo_bar_baz`) won't match. Use `replace(/_/g, '-')`.

`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201` — the array branch deletes `obj[k]` unconditionally and pushes possibly-`undefined` entries when `_lookupSubType` misses, unlike the singular branch which guards on `hydrated`. Filter out falsy results. Also `hydrated || []` is dead — `.map` always returns an array.

`app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:37` — after save, the category is re-derived from `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)`; when `categoryId` is null (server defaults to uncategorized) the row displays a blank category badge until reload. Prefer using the `category_id` returned in the save response.
`app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4-14` — all three method overrides are identical to the default `attributes` behavior and can be deleted.
`config/locales/client.en.yml` — `admin.embedding.edit` is defined but unused; `host: "Allowed Hosts"` is a plural label for a singular column key.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will drop the table if it already exists before creating it. This is a concrete, verifiable risk introduced by the diff and is generally not needed for a normal forward-only migration creating a new table.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code assigns `host.category_id = params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` and then saves without any validation that the referenced category actually exists. The `embeddable_hosts` table migration sets `category_id` to `null: false` but does not add a foreign key constraint, so an invalid/nonexistent `category_id` can be persisted, producing an orphaned association (`host.category` would be `nil`) and likely UI/API inconsistencies. The model only has `belongs_to :category` and no presence/existence validation, so this is not prevented at the application level either. The “no strong params permit” part is less compelling here since the controller is not mass-assigning attributes, but the missing category existence protection / FK-less orphan risk is a real, verifiable correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/adapters/rest.js.es6:22` — `type.replace('_', '-')` replaces only the first underscore; a future multi-word admin model (`foo_bar_baz`) won't match. Use `replace(/_/g, '-')`.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `basePath(store, type)` was changed to normalize a model name by doing `type.replace('_', '-')` before checking membership in `ADMIN_MODELS` (now including `embeddable-host`). For the admin models shown here (`plugin`, `site-customization`, `embeddable-host`), the corresponding underscored forms would have at most one underscore (`site_customization`, `embeddable_host`), so replacing only the first underscore is sufficient and does not create a verifiable bug for the code introduced/modified in this diff. The finding relies on a hypothetical future model name with multiple underscores, which is speculative and not demonstrated by the current changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/store.js.es6:196-201` — the array branch deletes `obj[k]` unconditionally and pushes possibly-`undefined` entries when `_lookupSubType` misses, unlike the singular branch which guards on `hydrated`. Filter out falsy results. Also `hydrated || []` is dead — `.map` always returns an array.

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js` the new plural `_id(s?)` handling does `obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` and then assigns the resulting array directly to `obj[pluralized]` while unconditionally `delete obj[k]`. If `_lookupSubType` returns `undefined`/`null` for any id (which the existing singular branch explicitly guards against), the array will contain falsy entries and the original id list is lost due to unconditional deletion. That is a concrete behavioral change and can produce incorrect hydrated results compared to the guarded singular branch. Also, `hydrated || []` is effectively redundant because `.map` always returns an array when it runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:37` — after save, the category is re-derived from `Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId)`; when `categoryId` is null (server defaults to uncategorized) the row displays a blank category badge until reload. Prefer using the `category_id` returned in the save response.

adjudication.rationale: In `embeddable-host.js.es6` the `save()` action sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and allows saving even when `categoryId` is `null` (since `cantSave` only checks host/isSaving). Server-side, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host` explicitly defaults a blank `category_id` to `SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id`. However, on successful save the client does `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')))`; if `categoryId` is `null` this will set `category` to `undefined`, so `{{category-badge host.category}}` will render blank until reload or further hydration. This is a verifiable mismatch introduced by the diff and aligns with the proposed finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:4-14` — all three method overrides are identical to the default `attributes` behavior and can be deleted.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHostSerializer`, the explicit `id`, `host`, and `category_id` methods simply return `object.id`, `object.host`, and `object.category_id`, which ActiveModel::Serializer (and Discourse’s ApplicationSerializer conventions) would already do when listed in `attributes`. Removing them would be a cleanup/refactor, not a bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the diff. The current code behaves correctly even if redundant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `config/locales/client.en.yml` — `admin.embedding.edit` is defined but unused; `host: "Allowed Hosts"` is a plural label for a singular column key.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `admin.embedding.edit` in `config/locales/client.en.yml`, but none of the added templates/components reference `i18n "admin.embedding.edit"` (they use `admin.embedding.host`, `category`, `add_host`, `confirm_delete`, `title`). So the key appears unused. However, an unused locale entry is not a functional/correctness defect introduced by the diff (it does not break behavior). The second claim (“host: 'Allowed Hosts' is a plural label for a singular column key”) is not a verifiable problem: the UI column represents a list of hosts and is rendered in a table iterating `embedding.embeddable_hosts`, so a plural label is reasonable and not incorrect.
